lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3, what is the difference between a fact and an opinion? (A fact can be checked; an opinion is what someone thinks.) Today: write an opinion that could change someone's mind.
Start with your opinion, clearly: "I think our town should build a skate park." Opinion words: I think, I believe, in my opinion, should.
Give two or three reasons, each in its own sentence or paragraph. A strong reason answers "Why?" and matters to your reader: "A skate park would give children a safe place to play."
Back each reason with facts and details: numbers, examples, what experts say. "The nearest park is 5 kilometres away, so many children have nowhere close to play."
Linking words join your opinion and reasons, so the reader can follow: for example, for instance, in addition, also, because, in order to, another reason is.
End with a conclusion that says your opinion again in new words. "For all these reasons, a skate park would make our town a better place." Start it with In conclusion or To sum up.

A worked example: "I believe every class should have a pet fish. First, fish are calm to watch. In addition, feeding them teaches us to care for animals. In conclusion, a fish would make our class happier."

picture.claim: Every class should have a pet fish.

lesson.text: Try it in the world: make a sign for your world's village that says why visitors should come, with three reasons and a strong ending. Next: research a topic and write a report.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence gives an opinion?
exercises.hint: Which one says what someone thinks?
exercises.explain: "I think ... should" gives an opinion. The others are facts you can check.
choices: I think playtime should be longer.

exercises.prompt: Which linking words add another reason?
exercises.hint: You want to say one more thing that supports your opinion.
exercises.explain: In addition adds another reason.

exercises.prompt: An opinion piece should end with a conclusion.
exercises.hint: How does a good opinion piece finish?
exercises.explain: True: the conclusion says the opinion again in new words.

exercises.prompt: Which words often begin an opinion?
exercises.hint: They tell the reader it is what you think.
exercises.explain: I believe, I think and in my opinion begin an opinion.

exercises.prompt: Put the opinion piece in order.
exercises.hint: Opinion first, then the reasons, then the ending.
exercises.explain: The opinion, the first reason, another reason, then the conclusion.
items: First, gardens teach us how food grows.
In conclusion, a garden would help every pupil.
In addition, working outside keeps us active.
I think every school should have a garden.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best reason for "Our class should visit the museum"?
exercises.hint: A good reason answers why, and matters to the reader.
exercises.explain: Seeing real fossils links to what the class is learning: a strong reason.
choices: We could see real fossils from our topic.

exercises.prompt: Which fact best backs up "We should cycle to school"?
exercises.hint: Which fact shows why cycling is good?
exercises.explain: Exercise keeps hearts healthy: a fact that supports the opinion.
choices: Cycling is exercise that keeps hearts healthy.

exercises.prompt: Choose the linking words: "Books teach us a lot. ___, a book about space can teach us about the planets."
exercises.hint: Is the second sentence an example of the first?
exercises.explain: A book about space is an example of books teaching us: For example.

exercises.prompt: Every reason in an opinion piece should support the opinion.
exercises.hint: What is a reason for?
exercises.explain: True: each reason should help show why the opinion is right.

exercises.prompt: Sort the linking words by their job.
exercises.hint: Does it add more, show an example, or finish?
exercises.explain: Add a reason: in addition, also. Give an example: for example, for instance. End: in conclusion, to sum up.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best conclusion?
exercises.hint: A conclusion says the opinion again.
exercises.explain: It sums up and says the opinion again in new words.
choices: For all these reasons, our town needs a library.
I went to a library once.

exercises.prompt: Which reason does NOT belong in "Our school should grow vegetables"?
exercises.hint: Which one has nothing to do with growing vegetables?
exercises.explain: A red car has nothing to do with vegetables. The other three are reasons that support the opinion.
choices: My uncle has a red car.
We would learn how food grows.
We could eat fresh, healthy food.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence gives an opinion and a reason?
exercises.hint: Look for what someone thinks, and for because.
exercises.explain: "Recycling matters" is the opinion, and "because it saves materials" is the reason.
choices: Recycling matters because it saves materials.

exercises.prompt: Fix the weak reason: "We should have a class pet because pets."
exercises.hint: A reason explains why the idea is good.
exercises.explain: Caring for a pet teaches responsibility: a real reason that supports the opinion.
choices: because caring for it teaches responsibility

exercises.prompt: A strong opinion piece gives just one reason, said many times.
exercises.hint: How many reasons make a strong case?
exercises.explain: False: two or three different reasons, each backed with facts, make a strong case.

exercises.prompt: Choose the linking words: "We need a bin in the park ___ keep it clean."
exercises.hint: The gap explains what the bin is for.
exercises.explain: In order to shows a purpose: the bin is there to keep the park clean.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence.
exercises.hint: Start with the words that show it is an opinion.
exercises.explain: In my opinion, reading is fun.

exercises.prompt: Match each linking phrase to its job.
exercises.hint: Which one could only come at the end?
exercises.explain: Firstly gives the first reason, furthermore adds another, and in conclusion starts the ending.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: an opinion, a reason or a fact?
items: I think we need a skate park.
It would give children a safe place to play.
The nearest park is 5 km away.
Books help us learn new words.
exercises.hint: An opinion says what you think, a reason says why, and a fact can be checked.
exercises.explain: Opinions: we need a skate park, libraries matter. Reasons: a safe place to play, books help us learn words. Facts: the park is 5 km away, the library has 2,000 books.

exercises.prompt: Put the skate park opinion piece in order.
items: In conclusion, a skate park would help our town.
I think our town should build a skate park.
It would give children a safe place to play.
The nearest park is 5 km away.
exercises.hint: Opinion, then a reason, then a fact that backs it, then the conclusion.
exercises.explain: State the opinion, give a reason (a safe place to play), back it with a fact (the nearest park is 5 km away), then end with a conclusion that says it again.
